title: Fylgja snapshot v2 — the core's one input and its probes (018, 016)
description: A snapshot is one JSON document wrapping an unchanged CTM 2 (ctm.schema.json): the core's one input (D-061). The server takes one for every twin create, intent read --out writes one, twin create --snapshot and twin compile --snapshot take one, and the store keeps each under snapshots/<snapshot_id>.json beside the bundles, never overwritten. The outer part is snapshot_version, snapshot_id and observed_at, the take's time; the body is ctm and probes, the probe declarations beside the intent. snapshot_id is the lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the body's canonical bytes with the inner envelope's observed_at left out and nothing else left out: the bytes the id hashes differ from the stored bytes, which keep observed_at and the outer part. The canonical bytes are the CTM's own form (ctm.Normalize, struct field order, two-space indent, LF, a trailing newline) wrapped as {"ctm": …, "probes": […]}, the probes in the declaration's order and each in its field order; by hand, jq --indent 2 'del(.snapshot_version, .snapshot_id, .observed_at, .ctm.envelope.observed_at)' snapshots/<id>.json | sha256sum, exact when no string holds <, >, &, U+2028 or U+2029, which Go's encoder escapes and jq writes raw, or DEL (U+007F), which jq escapes and Go writes raw. So the same intent taken twice has one id, whenever it was read, while the branch's history stands: a rebase re-stamps the branch and moves every stage's snapshot, and an artifact re-rendered to different bytes for unchanged data, never seen, would move it. A file a client sends may leave out snapshot_id, which the server computes, and observed_at, which it fills from the inner CTM; present, each is checked (snapshot.id.mismatch, snapshot.invalid). A document of another version than 1 or 2, or of none, is refused (snapshot.version.unsupported) and nothing converts one; the inner CTM is refused by its own rules, ctm.version.unsupported naming the file and data.required.missing naming the field prefixed ctm. A snapshot holds configuration, as the CTM does: it lives in the store and crosses as a file, never in a finding, a log line or a document. 016 moves it to version 2 (D-064): probes is the list of probe declarations, each element the declaration's probe (probes.schema.json's $defs/probe: a name, a format and two endpoints, each a device, an uncabled interface, an address with its prefix length and a gateway), [] when the take was given none, and hashed into the id as the empty list was, in its order; a take with a --probes file or the kind FylgjaProbe's objects carries them, and the compiler places each probe's two hosts under provenance synthesized, never in the CTM. Each element is decoded strictly and held to the declaration's rules that read no CTM before the snapshot is filed or compiled, the first fault refused as snapshot.invalid at probes[<i>].<field>: the shape this schema says, and four rules across fields that it cannot (probe.name.duplicate, probe.gateway.outside, probe.family.mixed, probe.address.duplicate), which the reader holds; whether a format is one a probe package declares is the server's, against the packages it loaded (probe.format.unknown). A document of version 1, which 018 wrote and 019's frozen copy of this contract describes, is read wherever a snapshot is read as a 2 with no probes, its probes list required and empty: the version is not hashed, so its id is unchanged and nothing is converted or re-filed. Every document Fylgja writes is a 2.

snapshot_version.description: 2, the version every document Fylgja writes declares. A 1 is read as a 2 with no probes and never written; it is 019's frozen copy's document, not this one's.

snapshot_id.description: The lowercase-hex SHA-256 of the hashed bytes: the body with the inner CTM's observed_at left out, in the canonical form the description gives. Required in a document Fylgja writes; optional in a file a client sends, computed when absent and checked when present. Not hashed.

observed_at.description: The UTC time the take began, six fractional digits, as the CTM envelope records a read's. A take is one read, so it equals ctm.envelope.observed_at; a file whose two differ is refused snapshot.invalid. Required in a document Fylgja writes; optional in a file a client sends, filled from the inner CTM when absent. Not hashed. Informational: it governs nothing (Constitution VI).

ctm.description: One CTM 2, unchanged by this feature: the reader's contract (D-057), which the compiler compiles. Hashed with its envelope's observed_at left out.

probes.description: The probe declarations, in the declaration's order: required, and [] for 'this intent, with no probe declarations'. Each element is the declaration's probe, held to its rules that read no CTM before filing (snapshot.invalid at probes[<i>].<field>). Hashed.
